significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish the form-(iii) law that “the pretraining checkpoint at which a belief becomes linearly decodable predicts the checkpoint at which that belief becomes context-unrevisable,” including an acquisition-before-entrenchment ordering beyond corpus frequency and item difficulty; this fixes expectations for the later revisability trajectory of facts measured earlier in training. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon—progressive loss of in-context override—and the form-(ii) mechanism that “attenuating” the strengthening parametric-recall component restores revisability, addressing the parametric-versus-context conflict documented by Xie et al.'s Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth rather than merely showing that beliefs are decodable. The branches are determinate and informative: failure of H1/H2 would rule out the proposed developmental coupling, while failure of H3 would preserve the temporal law but reject consolidation as its causal explanation. Topic substitution fails decisively: replacing the checkpoint ordering and predictive coupling with generic research on LLM beliefs would not merit this score, because the above cross-checkpoint law is substantially more constraining than the topic's obvious probe-and-steer hypothesis.

reach.justification: The principal handle is the claimed “per-fact acquisition timing predicts entrenchment timing,” supplemented by “checkpoint-aware RAG diagnostics” and a “context-vs-prior reliance” signal; it is ex ante because acquisition measurements can flag facts likely to become resistant to corrective context at later checkpoints, leaving a training-time action window. Unlike a model-specific direction alone, the partial predictive coupling is a relation that can be re-estimated on a new model while still predicting what should be found—acquisition-before-entrenchment and correlated timing beyond frequency and difficulty. The asserted scope covers factual contradiction tasks across Pythia and OLMo checkpoint families, with plausible uptake by model trainers and RAG auditors, although the claim itself concedes that results “may not transfer to other pretraining regimes or to very large closed models,” limiting broader deployment reach. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic LLM-belief research supplies neither the forward-looking checkpoint predictor nor the resulting training-time gating handle.
